official_measurement_examples.name: Planning standing advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's white-clawed-crayfish standing advice is a material planning consideration and was updated 7 April 2025.

official_measurement_examples.name: CL11 survey-only scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL11 permits specified white-clawed-crayfish survey methods and may inform development, but it does not permit translocation or holding crayfish while works are carried out.

official_measurement_examples.name: Crayfish-trap extra permission
official_measurement_examples.fact: Using a crayfish trap under CL11 also requires separate Environment Agency authorisation under the freshwater-fisheries regime.

official_measurement_examples.name: CL11 current period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current CL11 terms are valid from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030 and require registration plus recording and reporting.

official_measurement_examples.name: Development mitigation route
official_measurement_examples.fact: For Wildlife and Countryside Act schedule species without their own mitigation form, A05a is the overriding-public-interest route that includes development and requires supporting mitigation evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: CL23 maintenance distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL23 is a maintenance licence for moving white-clawed crayfish away from harm during specified water-body maintenance and is not a general development mitigation licence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Survey return requirement
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL11 survey users must report annually, including where no licensed action was taken, and survey reporting does not by itself establish current species absence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: White-clawed-crayfish survey, maintenance and mitigation licences do not themselves establish planning permission, ownership, access rights or parcel development capacity.

core_rules: white-clawed-crayfish standing advice is not proof crayfish are present on a parcel
white-clawed-crayfish survey result is not planning permission
planning permission is not A05a mitigation authority
CL11 survey authority is not development mitigation authority
CL23 maintenance authority is not development mitigation authority
CL11 trap authority does not replace separate Environment Agency permission where required
survey licence registration is not site approval
annual licence return is not proof of current species absence
historic survey evidence must retain date methods and watercourse scope
non-native crayfish findings must not be treated as white-clawed-crayfish evidence
biosecurity controls do not determine land ownership
mitigation licensing does not reserve development capacity
licence compliance does not create access rights
planning standing advice is not a planning decision
no parcel white-clawed-crayfish clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
